Today's verdict NEUTRAL-CAUTIOUS
When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **1**/10: price action calm, almost no crash signals triggered vs VIX Spike Tier **2**/4: **60%** spike probability, skew active, backwardation active
Price and the options market are running separate narratives. Trust the options market: backwardation means the front of the VIX curve is more expensive than the back, which hedgers pay for near-term protection rather than distant tail risk. When skew and backwardation are both live simultaneously, implied vol leads realized vol. The calm price action reflects where vol has been, not where options pricing says it is going.
Today's tension
Crash signals are absent but the options market is already hedging a vol expansion that price action has not confirmed
Bull
The Crash Index at **1/10** and a STABLE regime score of **28** say the underlying bid is intact. Options hedging at **60%** spike probability is precautionary, not distribution.
Bear
VIX backwardation and active skew at **60%** spike probability say someone is paying up for near-term coverage. Internally, **15** of **43** diverging pairs tilt bearish against just **4** bullish.
The tell: Whether HYG credit stress joins VIX backwardation to activate the T1 x HYG confluence. That pair firing confirms the options market is right and price is lagging.
AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The macro tape is calm on the surface and unsettled underneath. Crash Index at 1/10 and a STABLE regime score of 28 say no regime break is imminent. But MIXED bias means competing signals are pulling in opposite directions: 15 bearish diverging pairs against 4 bullish, VIX backwardation active, skew live, and macro regime confidence at just 45% for INFLATIONARY. That low conviction is itself a number to take seriously.

The 15-to-4 bearish skew in diverging pairs says you don't add to cyclical or small-cap exposure here. The 45% confidence in an inflationary macro regime barely edges over the alternatives and doesn't support a hard tilt into commodity or real asset longs. STABLE-with-MIXED means you hold what you own and don't extend.

The main risk is the options market forcing a realized vol catch-up. VIX at Tier 2 with 60% spike probability and both skew and backwardation active means the conditions for a vol expansion are assembled. The reading that flips the stance: HYG credit stress joining VIX backwardation to trigger T1 x HYG. Until that fires, the vol signal is a warning without a verdict.

Dow Theory generalized · cross-asset divergences
Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence here means pairs of assets that normally move together have broken their historical correlation, and correlation drift is the measured shift in that relationship over time. Of 43 tracked pairs, 44.18% are diverging right now, with 15 showing a bearish drift against just 4 bullish, a net bearish skew of 11 pairs.

The six deepest breaks have each scored 80 out of 100. The MOVE bond volatility index has decoupled from its counterpart, a correlation that shifted from +0.69 to near zero at +0.01: bond vol and equity vol are no longer moving as one.

Regional banks (KRE) are now moving opposite broad financials (XLF), a relationship that went from +0.08 to -0.56. Momentum (MTUM) has broken from the S&P 500 (SPY), drifting from +0.49 to -0.37: the stocks that led the market are no longer participating in its moves.

The composite zone reads CALM, meaning the share of diverging pairs hasn't crossed an alarm threshold. But the 15-to-4 bearish skew is what you weight: when this many pairs break at this depth simultaneously, the broad market lacks a coherent internal structure.

Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Korea's KOSPI leads all regions at +7.4% over five days against a broadly defensive global backdrop. Australia's ASX is down -0.7% over the same stretch.

Europe is uniformly soft: STOXX50E down -0.8% and the Swiss SMI down -3.9% over five days. In the US, the Nasdaq 100 is barely red at -0.1% while the Russell 2000 is down -2.1%: large-cap tech is the only segment holding the US market together.

That pattern (large-cap steady, small-cap lagging) repeats across every region and points to a defensive quality rotation, not broad risk-on buying. Crypto confirms the lean: ETH down -1.6% and SOL down -4.0% over five days, consistent with the same risk-off pressure visible across equities.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 1/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

Crash Index at 1/10 means almost no individual crash signals have triggered. VIX Spike sits at Tier 2 of 4 with 60% spike probability, skew active, and backwardation active.

These two readings are coherent: the Crash Index measures realized-side inputs (price drawdown, breadth deterioration, credit stress), while the VIX spike detector reads the options market's forward expectation. Backwardation means the front of the VIX curve is more expensive than the back, which hedgers pay for near-term protection.

Price is calm; implied vol is not. This is the normal sequence before a vol expansion materializes: options lead, then realized vol catches up.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 1/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

Emerging industries: high velocity = screener scores accelerating this week vs prior baseline — potential early rotation signal.
Competitor themes: token frequency × recency across top finance Substacks — useful narrative context, not a trading signal.
Best R/R: only entries with an active screener leg (PULLBACK / BOTTOM / SMART_MONEY_SURGE etc.). EV% = probabilistic edge per trade. Cross-check with weekly chart before sizing.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
